input.quote: Section 8.3 Termination. This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full (Section 8.3) — far longer than twelve months — yet our only exit against the Servicer is the for-cause removal in Section 7.2(c), exercisable by the Indenture Trustee only upon a continuing Servicer Termination Event. Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are Class A Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption mechanics, not a convenience exit for us. There is therefore no Customer convenience termination right at all, which fails both preferred and fallback (fallback element 1 is absent and there is no early-termination fee to cap). We target preferred because Section 7.1 already bars the Servicer from resigning absent legal inability, so the Vendor-side element is met, and the fallback would concede a Servicer term-end exit on 90 days' notice that the contract currently forecloses. New Section 7.7 designates the Issuer as the "Customer" for the Servicer's services and gives it an unconditional 30-day convenience termination with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees; the conforming words in Section 8.3 keep the natural-expiry formula consistent with that exit. Sections 7.3 and 7.4 already operate on any termination "under this Agreement", so continued-performance and successor-servicer mechanics engage without further edits.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "the Servicer grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their respective Affiliates, a license to use its processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications..." — Affiliates are within the grant (albeit conditioned on written notice, which satisfies the fallback formulation).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant runs only to "the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their respective Affiliates". The phrase "or to have serviced, the Receivables" describes permitted purpose, not a grant of rights to contractors; no express extension to contractors or subservicers acting on Issuer/Depositor's behalf appears. Drafter concedes contractor coverage was not added.

elements.element: A paid-up licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The inserted grant is silent on consideration and duration; it is characterised neither as paid-up nor as subscription, and no perpetuity language ("perpetual", "for so long as") is present. Whether the paid-up condition is triggered cannot be determined from the operative text.

elements.element: A paid-up licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No "irrevocable" (or "non-revocable") wording in the inserted sentence, and the text does not identify the licence as paid-up, so the condition's applicability is indeterminate. Note the retained sentence contains no at-will revocation right, so nothing expressly permits Servicer revocation.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the grant is a servicing-purpose licence under a transfer and servicing agreement with no subscription, fee or term structure attached to it, so no subscription-licence termination standard is required.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Transferability is confined to "a successor of the Issuer or the Depositor by merger or acquisition" — narrower than transferability to successors generally (e.g. successors by operation of law, reorganisation or asset sale).

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "the Servicer grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their respective Affiliates, a license to use..."; "Affiliate" is a defined term (p0579), so no undefined capitalised term is introduced.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "...which license is transferable to a successor of the Issuer or the Depositor by merger or acquisition."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language (Affiliates on written notice; transferability to an M&A successor of the Issuer or Depositor). The finding is therefore position-complete at the declared fallback target.

Preferred level is not complete. To reach it the drafter would need to (a) extend the grant expressly to "contractors and subservicers acting on the Issuer's or Depositor's behalf", (b) make the licence "perpetual and irrevocable" (or state it is fully paid-up and perpetual/irrevocable), and (c) broaden transferability from "a successor by merger or acquisition" to "Customer's successors and permitted assigns". These are noted, not required, since the fallback is satisfied.

Minimality holds: the change is a single added sentence for a clause that did not exist; the Servicer's existing carve-out (Successor Servicer, third parties, transfer/confidentiality restrictions and legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection protections) is retained verbatim with no deletions. "Customer" (Issuer/Depositor) is not defined to include Affiliates, so the affiliate extension is not duplicative.

The "Notwithstanding the preceding sentence" opener is narrowly targeted at the immediately preceding no-obligation-to-license sentence and is necessary to avoid a directly contradictory retained sentence; it is not a broad override of the transition provisions and so does not fail minimality.

Intent is preserved: the Section 7.4/7.5 transition allocation, delivery obligations and the Servicer's restricted-materials protections survive, subordinated only to the extent of the new grant by the express priority language; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created.

Residual drafting point (not a defect at the fallback): the grant's purpose scope "as necessary to service, or to have serviced, the Receivables" combined with the retained Successor Servicer carve-out could be read as leaving downstream use by a Successor Servicer contested; the notwithstanding clause resolves priority, but express contractor/subservicer wording would remove the ambiguity.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.5(a): "On its resignation or termination, the Servicer will cooperate with the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in effecting ... an orderly transition"; 7.5(b) likewise runs from "the effective date of its resignation or termination". Resignation and termination are the only end-of-engagement events for the Servicer under this servicing structure (there is no separate servicer 'expiry' concept), so every covered ending is captured, and the inserted sentence uses the same trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence commits only to "at least ninety (90) days after the effective date of its resignation or termination"; no six-month period appears anywhere in Section 7.5 or 7.3.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No rate mechanic was added. Retained 7.5(c) runs the other way (transition expenses of the Issuer/trustees/Successor Servicer are "paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer"); there is no then-current-rates pricing for the assistance.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "in any event will deliver the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer to the Successor Servicer no later than thirty (30) days after such effective date" — a hard 30-day outside date measured from the effective date of resignation or termination, backstopping the retained "as soon as practicable" standard.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The insertion is silent on format; retained 7.5(b) only requires delivery of "the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer" with no commonly used, machine-readable format requirement.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written certification obligation exists in Section 7.5 as rendered; nothing was added.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same retained trigger in 7.5(a)/(b) ("On its resignation or termination" / "after the effective date of its resignation or termination"), and the inserted period is anchored to that identical effective date, so the assistance period applies after every covered ending, not merely an anticipated one.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The predecessor Servicer will provide the transition assistance described in this Section 7.5 for at least ninety (90) days after the effective date of its resignation or termination." The scope is defined by reference to the cooperation and transfer duties in Section 7.5, so the trigger and content are not undefined. Section 7.3 (performance of servicing until a Successor Servicer accepts, or the date in the termination notice) addresses continued servicing rather than transition assistance and does not contradict the new floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted 30-day outside date for delivery of the Receivable Files and the accounts and records to the Successor Servicer (the transferee engaged by the Issuer under Section 7.4), replacing reliance on the open-ended "as soon as practicable" standard for timing purposes.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies the two missing fallback terms (a 90-day minimum assistance period and a 30-day outside date for delivery of the Receivable Files and records), while the trigger element was already satisfied by retained Section 7.5(a)/(b).

Preferred level is not reached. To reach it the drafter would need to (i) extend assistance to up to six (6) months, (ii) state that assistance is at the Servicer's then-current rates, (iii) require delivery in a commonly used, machine-readable format, and (iv) add a post-return deletion and written certification obligation. The finding correctly does not claim these.

Minimality holds: nothing was deleted (the "as soon as practicable" standard, the processes/models/servicing-software carve-back and the 7.5(c) expense allocation all survive), no format, deletion, survival tail, expense or procedural extras were added, and the addition is confined to the two fallback elements actually missing.

Intent is preserved: the 30-day date operates as a backstop to the retained "as soon as practicable" duty in 7.5(b)(ii) rather than replacing it, and Section 7.3's continued-performance mechanic is untouched. One drafting watch-point only (not a failure): the phrase "in any event" sits alongside the retained sentence relieving the Servicer of any obligation to provide items "covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies" — since the primary 7.5(b)(ii) delivery duty already coexists with that carve-back, no new conflict is created, but adding "subject to the last sentence of Section 7.5(b)" would remove any argument of inconsistency.
Classification as a deviation is right: without the insertion the clause failed the fallback on two material terms (no minimum assistance period; no outside date for data delivery).

input.quote: Section 8.3 Termination. This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full (Section 8.3) — far longer than twelve months — yet the only exits are the Indenture Trustee's for-cause removal on a continuing Servicer Termination Event (Section 7.2(c)) and natural run-off. Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are Class A Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption mechanics, not a convenience exit for us. No Customer convenience termination right exists, failing both preferred and fallback (fallback element 1 is absent; there is no early-termination fee to cap). We target preferred: Section 7.1 already bars the Servicer from resigning absent legal inability, so the Vendor-side element is met, and the fallback would concede a Servicer term-end exit on 90 days' notice that the contract currently forecloses. New Section 7.7 designates the Issuer as the "Customer" and gives it an unconditional 30-day convenience termination with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees; the Section 8.3 edits add that exit to the termination list and reletter it cleanly as (a)/(b)/(c). We deliberately did not condition our exit on appointment of a Successor Servicer — that would qualify the unconditional right the checklist requires — and Sections 7.3/7.4 already engage on any termination "under this Agreement".

ops.text: Section 7.7 Termination for Convenience. The Issuer (the "Customer" for the Servicer's services) may terminate this Agreement and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, in which case the Servicer will refund to the Customer pro rata any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of the termination.

We conformed Section 8.3's termination list to include that exit; Section 7.1's no-resignation bar on the Servicer is untouched.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A, together with Verizon ABS LLC (Issuer and Depositor); counterparty is Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless (Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."

This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement."},{"id":"p0351","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","text":"(a) Optional Acquisition. On each Payment Date following the last day of a Collection Period as of which the aggregate Principal Balance of the Receivables shall be equal to or less than 10% of the aggregate Principal Balance of the Receivables as of the Closing Date, the Class A Certificateholder (for as long as the Class A Certificateholder is an Originator or an Affiliate of the Originators), with the consent of the Administrator, on behalf of the Issuer, shall have the option to acquire, as of the end of the immediately preceding Collection Period, any Receivables remaining in the Trust Property on such date by transferring to the Issuer an amount equal to the Optional Acquisition Amount (the \"Optional Acquisition\"), and to redeem the Notes, in whole but not in part (the \"Clean-Up Redemption\") without any Make-Whole Payment (other than any Make-Whole Payments already due and payable on such date)."},{"id":"p0354","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","text":"After receiving such notice, the Indenture Trustee will promptly notify the Noteholders of the resulting Clean-Up Redemption and provide instructions for surrender of the Notes for final payment including all accrued and unpaid interest and any applicable Make-Whole Payments already due and payable on the Notes, as set forth in Section 10.1(a) of the Indenture."},{"id":"p0358","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","text":"(a) Optional Redemption. On any Payment Date on and after the Payment Date in February 2021, the Class A Certificateholder (for as long as the Class A Certificateholder is an Originator or an Affiliate of the Originators), with the consent of the Administrator, on behalf of the Issuer, shall have the option to redeem the Notes, in whole but not in part (the \"Optional Redemption\"), with a required Make-Whole Payment."},{"id":"p0359","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","text":"(b) Exercise of Optional Redemption. The Class A Certificateholder may exercise its option set forth in Section 8.2(a) by notifying the Issuer, the Servicer, the Indenture Trustee, the Owner Trustee and the Rating Agencies, in writing, at least ten (10) days before the Payment Date on which the Optional Redemption is to be exercised. After receiving such notice, the Indenture Trustee will promptly notify the Noteholders of the Optional Redemption and provide instructions for surrender of the Notes for final payment including all accrued and unpaid interest and any applicable Make-Whole Payments due and payable on the Notes, as set forth in Section 10.1(a) of the Indenture."},{"id":"p0286","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","text":"(d) Force Majeure. Neither the Servicer nor the Marketing Agent will be responsible or liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Agreement caused by, directly or indirectly, forces beyond its control, including strikes, work stoppages, acts of war, terrorism, civil or military disturbances, fire, flood, earthquakes, storms, hurricanes or other natural disasters or failures of mechanical, electronic or communication systems; provided, however that this provision shall not limit the right to remove the Servicer for a Servicer Termination Event as provided in Section 7.2(a), other than with respect to the extension of the grace periods as provided in Section 7.2(a). Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, as applicable, will use commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance as soon as practicable in the circumstances."}]

The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement. The Servicer will notify the Issuer, the Parent Support Provider, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee of its resignation as soon as practicable after it determines it is required to resign, together with an Opinion of Counsel supporting its determination. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement or in any other Transaction Document, immediately upon the resignation of Cellco as Servicer pursuant to this Section 7.1, Cellco, in its individual capacity, will be required to assume the obligations of the Servicer to acquire Receivables as set forth in Sections 3.4 and 4.7 of the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement and Sections 2.5 and 2.6 of this Agreement without further action."},{"id":"p0317","text":"Section 7.2 Servicer Termination Events."},{"id":"p0318","text":"(a) Servicer Termination Events. The following events will each be a \"Servicer Termination Event\":"},{"id":"p0319","text":"(i) (x) the Servicer fails to deposit, or deliver to the Owner Trustee or the Indenture Trustee for deposit, any Collections required to be delivered under this Agreement;"},{"id":"p0320","text":"(y) so long as Cellco is the Servicer, the Marketing Agent fails to deposit, or to cause the related Originators to deposit, into the Collection Account any Upgrade Payments required to be delivered under this Agreement, or (z) so long as Cellco is the Servicer, the Parent Support Provider fails to make any payments with respect to the items set forth in clause (x) or clause (y) above, to the extent the Servicer, or the Marketing Agent or any related Originator, respectively, fails to do so, and, in each case, which such failure continues for five (5) Business Days after the Servicer, the Marketing Agent or the Parent Support Provider, as applicable, receives written notice of the failure from the Owner Trustee or the Indenture Trustee, or a Responsible Person of the Servicer, the Marketing Agent or the Parent Support Provider, as applicable, obtains actual knowledge of the failure; or"},{"id":"p0321","text":"(ii) the Servicer (including in its capacity as Custodian) fails to observe or to perform any obligation under this Agreement, other than as set forth in clause (i) or (iii), which failure has a material adverse effect on the Noteholders and continues for ninety (90) days after the Servicer receives written notice of the failure from the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee or the Noteholders of at least a majority of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class; or"},{"id":"p0322","text":"(iii) so long as Cellco is the Servicer, the failure by (x) the Marketing Agent to make, or to cause the related Originators to make, (i) any payments required to be paid by the Marketing Agent, including without limitation Credit Payments or (ii) payments relating to the acquisition by the Marketing Agent or the related Originators of Receivables that are subject to certain transfers, but not including Upgrade Payments, or (y) the Parent Support Provider to make any payments set forth in clause (x) above, to the extent that the Marketing Agent or any related Originator fails to do so, and in either case, that continues for ten (10) Business Days after the Marketing Agent or Parent Support Provider, as applicable, receives written notice of the failure from the Owner Trustee or the Indenture Trustee, or a Responsible Person of the Marketing Agent or the Parent Support Provider, as applicable, obtains actual knowledge of the failure; or"},{"id":"p0323","text":"(iv) an Insolvency Event of the Servicer occurs;"},{"id":"p0324","text":"33"},{"id":"p0325","text":"provided, however, that a delay or failure of performance referred to in clauses (i), (ii) or (iii) above for an additional period of sixty (60) days will not constitute a Servicer Termination Event if such delay or failure was caused by force majeure or other similar occurrence, as further described in Section 6.2(d)."},{"id":"p0326","text":"(b) Notice of Servicer Termination Event. The Servicer will notify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee of any Servicer Termination Event or any event that with the giving of notice or passage of time, or both, would become a Servicer Termination Event, no later than five (5) Business Days after a Responsible Person of the Servicer has received written notice of or has actual knowledge of the event. If a Servicer Termination Event occurs, the Issuer will promptly notify the Rating Agencies and the Asset Representations Reviewer."},{"id":"p0327","text":"(c) Removal. If a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing, the Indenture Trustee may and, if directed by the Noteholders of a majority of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class, must remove the Servicer and terminate its rights and obligations under this Agreement by notifying the Servicer, the Issuer, the Parent Support Provider, the Owner Trustee, and the Secured Parties. The notice of termination will state the date the termination will be effective. On receipt of the notice, the Issuer will promptly notify the Rating Agencies, and the Owner Trustee will promptly notify the Certificateholders. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement or in any other Transaction Document, immediately upon the removal of Cellco as Servicer pursuant to this Section 7.2, Cellco, in its individual capacity, shall assume the obligations of the Servicer to acquire Receivables as set forth in Sections 3.4 and 4.7 of the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement and Sections 2.5 and 2.6 of this Agreement without further action."},{"id":"p0328","text":"(d) Waiver of Servicer Termination Events. The Noteholders of a majority of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class or, if no Notes are Outstanding, the Owner Trustee, at the direction of the Class A Certificateholder, may direct the Indenture Trustee to waive a Servicer Termination Event, except with respect to a failure to make required deposits to or payment from any of the Bank Accounts, and the consequences thereof. Upon the waiver, the Servicer Termination Event will be deemed not to have occurred. No waiver will extend to any other Servicer Termination Event or impair a right relating to any other Servicer Termination Event. The Issuer will promptly notify the Rating Agencies of any waiver."},{"id":"p0329","text":"Section 7.3 Continue to Perform. If the Servicer resigns under Section 7.1, it will continue to perform its obligations as Servicer under this Agreement until the earlier to occur of (a) a Successor Servicer accepting its engagement as Servicer under Section 7.4 or (b) the date the Servicer is legally unable to act as Servicer. If the Servicer is terminated under this Agreement, it will continue to perform its obligations as Servicer under this Agreement until the date stated in the notice of termination. If Cellco is the resigning or removed Servicer, Cellco shall (x) remit any amounts due on the Receivables that are remitted to Cellco in error, rather than to the Successor Servicer as set forth in the notice sent to Obligors under Section 3.13, and provide the Successor Servicer with any necessary information regarding the amount remitted to the Successor Servicer by Cellco and the Receivable for which such amount was remitted and (y) continue to perform its remittance obligations set forth in Section 3.12(b) for as long as any"},{"id":"p0330","text":"34"},{"id":"p0331","text":"Receivable continues to have a Principal Balance or until this Agreement is terminated as set forth in Section 8.3."},{"id":"p0332","text":"Section 7.4 Successor Servicer."},{"id":"p0333","text":"(a) Engagement of Successor Servicer; Indenture Trustee to Act."},{"id":"p0334","text":"(i) If the Servicer resigns or is terminated under this Agreement, the Indenture Trustee will promptly engage an institution having a net worth of not less than $50,000,000 whose regular business and operations includes the servicing of consumer receivables and can accommodate the servicing of device payment plan agreements, as the successor to the Servicer under this Agreement (the \"Successor Servicer\") and successor to the Administrator under Section 3.4 of the Administration Agreement."},{"id":"p0335","text":"(ii) If no Person has accepted the engagement as Successor Servicer when the Servicer stops performing its obligations, the Indenture Trustee, without further action, will be automatically appointed the Successor Servicer to perform the obligations of the Servicer (other than any obligations specifically excluded) until such time as another Successor Servicer shall accept engagement as Successor Servicer. If the Indenture Trustee becomes the Successor Servicer, it (A) will do so in its individual capacity and not in its capacity as Indenture Trustee and, accordingly, Article VI of the Indenture will be inapplicable to the Indenture Trustee solely in its capacity as Successor Servicer and (B) may appoint as Servicer any one of its Affiliates, but the Indenture Trustee, in its capacity as Successor Servicer, will be liable for the actions and omissions of such Affiliate. If the Indenture Trustee is unwilling or legally unable to act as Successor Servicer, it will appoint, or petition a court of competent jurisdiction to appoint, an institution having a net worth of not less than $50,000,000 whose regular business and operations includes the servicing of consumer receivables and can accommodate the servicing of device payment plan agreements, as successor to the Servicer under this Agreement. The Indenture Trustee will be released from its obligations as Successor Servicer on the date that a new Servicer accepts its engagement as Successor Servicer."},{"id":"p0336","text":"(b) Acceptance of Engagement. The Successor Servicer will accept its engagement by assuming the Servicer's obligations under this Agreement or entering into an amendment to this Agreement or a new servicing agreement on substantially the same terms as this Agreement, in a form acceptable to the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee. The Successor Servicer will deliver a copy of the assumption, amendment or new servicing agreement to the other parties and the Indenture Trustee. The Successor Servicer (other than the Indenture Trustee as Successor Servicer) will accept its engagement as Administrator according to Section 3.5 of the Administration Agreement. Promptly following a Successor Servicer's acceptance of its engagement, the Indenture Trustee will notify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Secured Parties of the engagement. On receipt of a notice of engagement, the Issuer will promptly notify the Rating Agencies and the Asset Representations Reviewer, and the Owner Trustee will promptly notify the Certificateholders. Any Successor Servicer will agree to provide to Cellco any information relating to payments received from Obligors (including any payments received on a Receivable that was the subject of an upgrade for which none of the Marketing Agent, the related Originator or the Parent Support Provider deposited a required Upgrade Payment),"},{"id":"p0337","text":"35"},{"id":"p0338","text":"delinquencies in payments by Obligors, any Written-Off Receivables and any other information related to the Obligors and the Receivables required by Cellco to service the accounts of which any Receivables are a part, including, but not limited to, granting and applying credits to any account for which none of the Marketing Agent, the related Originator or the Parent Support Provider remitted an Upgrade Payment, as set forth in Section 3.12(b). Any Successor Servicer will agree to be bound by the terms and conditions of the legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection policies set forth in Exhibit A attached hereto to the extent such Successor Servicer receives information from Cellco or any of its Affiliates relating to the Receivables. For the avoidance of doubt, no Successor Servicer will be required to assume or undertake the obligations of Cellco, as Servicer, under Sections 3.4 and 4.7 of the Master Trust Receivables Transfer Agreement or Sections 2.5 and 2.6 of this Agreement. No Successor Servicer shall have any liability for the acts or omissions of any predecessor Servicer."},{"id":"p0339","text":"(c) Compensation of Successor Servicer. The Indenture Trustee may make arrangements for the compensation of the Successor Servicer out of Collections as it and the Successor Servicer may agree. In addition to the Servicing Fee, on the date of its appointment as Successor Servicer, such Successor Servicer will receive a fee of $150,000 payable pursuant to Section 8.2(c) or 8.2(e) of the Indenture, as applicable, and thereafter, will be entitled to the Additional Successor Servicer Fee, which will be paid in accordance with the priorities set forth in Section 8.2(c) or 8.2(e) of the Indenture, as applicable."},{"id":"p0340","text":"(d) Transfer of Authority. On the effective date of the Servicer's resignation or termination or the later date that the Servicer stops performing its obligations, and solely to the extent the Successor Servicer is an entity other than the Indenture Trustee, all rights and obligations of the Servicer under this Agreement and of the Administrator under the Administration Agreement will become the rights and obligations of the Successor Servicer, including as successor Administrator. For the avoidance of doubt, (x) the resignation or removal of Cellco as Servicer will not result in the termination of Cellco's duties as Marketing Agent and (y) if the Indenture Trustee is the Successor Servicer, Cellco will continue to act as Administrator under the Administration Agreement, to the extent it is able to continue to perform thereunder pursuant to the terms of the Administration Agreement."},{"id":"p0341","text":"(e) Authority of Issuer and Indenture Trustee. The Issuer and the Indenture Trustee are authorized to execute and deliver, on behalf of the Servicer, as attorney-in-fact or otherwise, all documents, and to do all other acts or things necessary or advisable to effect the termination and replacement of the Servicer."},{"id":"p0342","text":"Section 7.5 Transition of Servicing."},{"id":"p0343","text":"(a) Cooperation on Termination. On its resignation or termination, the Servicer will cooperate with the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in effecting (i) the termination of its rights and obligations under this Agreement and (ii) an orderly transition of such rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer."},{"id":"p0344","text":"(b) Transfer of Cash, Receivable Files and Records. As soon as practicable after the effective date of its resignation or termination, the predecessor Servicer will (i) transfer to the Successor Servicer all funds relating to the Receivables that are held or later received by the"},{"id":"p0345","text":"36"},{"id":"p0346","text":"predecessor Servicer and (ii) deliver to the Successor Servicer the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer. The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies."},{"id":"p0347","text":"(c) Expenses of Servicing Transition. All reasonable expenses incurred by the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in connection with (i) the transition of servicing rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer and (ii) amending this Agreement or entering into an assumption agreement or new agreement to reflect a succession of the Servicer will be paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer on receipt of an invoice in reasonable detail."},{"id":"p0348","text":"Section 7.6 Merger, Consolidation, Succession or Assignment. Any Person (a) into which the Servicer is merged or consolidated, (b) resulting from a merger or consolidation to which the Servicer is a party, (c) succeeding to the Servicer's business or (d) that is an Affiliate of the Servicer to whom the Servicer has assigned this Agreement, will be the successor to the Servicer under this Agreement. This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full (Section 8.3) — well beyond twelve months — yet the only exit against the Servicer is the for-cause removal right in Section 7.2(c), exercisable by the Indenture Trustee upon a continuing Servicer Termination Event. Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption mechanics, not a convenience termination right for us. There is therefore no Customer convenience exit at all, which fails both the preferred and fallback positions (fallback element 1 is likewise absent, and there is no early-termination fee to cap). We target the preferred level: Section 7.1 already bars the Servicer from resigning absent legal inability, so the Vendor-side element is met and the fallback (which would let the Servicer walk at term end on 90 days' notice) would weaken us. The single inserted Section 7.7 supplies the Issuer's 30-day convenience right and pro rata refund of prepaid fees; existing Sections 7.3 and 7.4 already handle continued performance and successor engagement on any termination "under this Agreement", so no consequential edits are needed.

content.text:
Resubmitted with the drafting cleanup applied.

**What changed this round:**
- **Section 8.3 relettered cleanly** — the amended sentence now reads "the earliest to occur of **(a)** a termination under Section 7.7, **(b)** the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full ... and **(c)** the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement." Two tight replacements handle the insertion and the (b)→(c) renumber; every other word of the clause is preserved verbatim.

**What I declined, and why:**
- **Conditioning the exit on appointment of a Successor Servicer.** That would convert the preferred element's *unconditional* Customer convenience right into a qualified one, handing the Servicer a practical veto over our exit — a weakening of our position and a term outside the checklist. Sections 7.3 and 7.4 already require the Servicer to continue performing until the date stated in the notice and oblige the Indenture Trustee to engage (or become) a Successor Servicer on any termination "under this Agreement", so the transition concern is already covered by retained language. Worth raising as a negotiation point if the Servicer or a Rating Agency pushes back, but not something to concede in our first draft.

**Position held:** preferred level; element 4 `already_met` on retained Section 7.1; no "in whole or in part", no survival tail, expense, procedure or extra remedy; Sections 7.2(c), 7.3, 7.4 and 7.6 untouched. The deterministic "Customer convenience termination present: false" reflects the pre-redline document — which is precisely the deviation being cured.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:

Finding rationale:
The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full (Section 8.3) — far longer than twelve months — yet the only exits are the Indenture Trustee's for-cause removal on a continuing Servicer Termination Event (Section 7.2(c)) and natural run-off. Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are Class A Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption mechanics, not a convenience exit for us. No Customer convenience termination right exists, failing both preferred and fallback (fallback element 1 is absent; there is no early-termination fee to cap). We target preferred: Section 7.1 already bars the Servicer from resigning absent legal inability, so the Vendor-side element is met, and the fallback would concede a Servicer term-end exit on 90 days' notice that the contract currently forecloses. New Section 7.7 designates the Issuer as the "Customer" and gives it an unconditional 30-day convenience termination with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees; the Section 8.3 edits add that exit to the termination list and reletter it cleanly as (a)/(b)/(c). We deliberately did not condition our exit on appointment of a Successor Servicer — that would qualify the unconditional right the checklist requires — and Sections 7.3/7.4 already engage on any termination "under this Agreement".

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: Section 7.7 supplies an unconditional Customer (Issuer) convenience right at 30 days' written notice with an express pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and retained Section 7.1 leaves the Servicer with no convenience exit during the term.

The failed regex "Customer convenience termination present" is a naming artifact, not a substantive gap — the right is granted to "The Issuer (the "Customer" for the Servicer's services)" in Section 7.7.

Minimality holds: three operations only (insert Section 7.7; add the Section 7.7 exit to Section 8.3; reletter (a)/(b)/(c) and change "earlier" to "earliest"). The Section 8.3 conforming edit is necessary because Section 8.3's exhaustive termination list would otherwise contradict the new exit. No survival tails, expense language, damages categories or unrelated deletions were added; Section 7.1 and Section 7.2(c) are untouched.

Intent is not preserved: by routing the new exit through Section 8.3(a), a unilateral 30-day notice from the Issuer terminates the entire multi-party Transfer and Servicing Agreement — not just the servicing engagement — while Notes remain Outstanding and Receivables unserviced. Repair: scope Section 7.7 (and the new Section 8.3(a)) to termination of the Servicer's appointment/servicing role rather than of "this Agreement", or expressly preserve the Agreement as to the Depositor, Custodian and Marketing Agent roles.

Related contradiction to repair in operative language: the defined term "Servicer" means "Cellco or any Successor Servicer engaged under Section 7.4 of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement", and Sections 7.3/7.4 presuppose the Agreement continuing so a Successor Servicer can be engaged and transition performed. If Section 8.3(a) terminates the Agreement on the Issuer's notice, that machinery is inoperative. Either tie the effective date of the Section 7.7 termination to the appointment of a Successor Servicer under Section 7.4 (a timing mechanic, not a consent condition, so the election remains unconditional), or add an express carve-out that Sections 7.3 and 7.4 continue to apply to a Section 7.7 termination.

Drafting nit (not a level failure): Section 7.7 coins the term "Customer" solely for use within that section; confirm it does not collide with any other defined term and consider using "the Issuer" throughout to avoid an orphan definition. Also note that the Servicing Fee is paid monthly out of collections, so the prepaid-fee refund will rarely bite — harmless, but the exit's value rests on the termination right itself.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-lol-cap-f2076103","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"The liability architecture sits at or above the fallback on its material terms, so we do not redline it. (1) Mutuality: Section 6.2(a) (Servicer/Marketing Agent, p0283) and Section 5.2(a) (Depositor, p0243) are parallel \"liable only for specific obligations\" waivers, and our entities have the additional benefit of Section 9.6 limited recourse (p0378, claims against Depositor/Issuer limited to the Depositor Transferred Property) and Section 9.7 (p0381-p0382). Our side's exposure is therefore effectively bounded while the counterparty's is not. (2) Cap basis: there is no monetary or fee-based cap anywhere in the document — searches for \"exceed\"/aggregate-liability language return no cap, and the Servicing Fee (p0975) is never used as a liability ceiling. The fallback's \"12 months of fees\" cap exists to floor Vendor exposure; here Cellco's exposure in amount is unlimited, which exceeds the fallback and benefits us, so we do not introduce a cap that would only weaken our position. (3) Carve-outs: because no cap exists, indemnification (Section 6.3, p0291-p0292), confidentiality/data-protection breaches (Exhibit A policies, p0146), gross negligence and willful misconduct all carry unlimited exposure, and gross negligence, bad faith and willful misconduct are the express standards of Servicer liability and indemnity. Minor shortfalls of the preferred wording — no general mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (the only such bar, p0469, binds the arbitral panel), no USD 1,000,000 floor, and no express \"payment obligations are not damages\" statement — are noted rather than flagged; the first two are only meaningful alongside a cap, and none is a material failure of the fallback. We note for the record (outside this rule) that Section 6.2(a) limits Cellco's liability to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, excluding ordinary negligence; that is a standard-of-care point, is mirrored for the Depositor, and is market standard for this securitization structure rather than a cap deviation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-fa8e5a87","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ X MISCELLANEOUS","rationale":"Section 10.2(a) conditions assignment on consent of the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and Controlling Class Noteholders, but not of the Issuer or Depositor, and it carries no reasonableness standard; and the carve-out for Section 7.6 lets the Servicer assign the Agreement outright to any Affiliate of Cellco (clause (d)) with no consent from us at all. That fails the fallback (no \"not unreasonably withheld\" standard, and a retained no-consent affiliate assignment route) and the preferred position. Our own side is already well placed: Section 5.3 gives the Depositor successor status on merger, consolidation, succession to its business or assignment to an Affiliate, and Section 7.1 permits the Servicer to resign only if it is legally unable to perform, so no Servicer exit is triggered by a change of control on our side. The edit therefore only tightens the Servicer's side — Issuer consent (not unreasonably withheld) plus a competitor bar — and leaves Section 5.3 untouched. No competitor definition is added; the term is used in its ordinary sense, which we consider sufficient here.","proposal":"Require Issuer consent (not unreasonably withheld) for any Servicer assignment, including the Section 7.6(d) Affiliate route, and bar assignment to a competitor.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-e0d58bb3","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on our side, so it meets the preferred position. Section 3.1 (p0080) and the parallel Custodian (p0137) and Marketing Agent (p0150) provisions are bare appointments of Cellco: none designates Cellco as sole or exclusive provider, and none bars the Issuer, Depositor or Indenture Trustee from engaging other providers. The Successor Servicer regime (p0335) affirmatively contemplates engaging a different servicer, confirming the absence of any lock-in. The word \"exclusive\" appears only in the Cap Collateral Account control mechanic (p0387-p0388), which is a control right held by the Issuer and therefore benefits our party, and in \"nonexclusive jurisdiction\" (p0427), a forum term. Searches for requirements-purchase, sole-source, \"any third party\" procurement bars and non-compete covenants returned nothing binding our party. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-9ae27f96","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"Section 6.3 contains a Servicer/Marketing Agent (vendor-side) indemnity in our favour, but it is limited to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence and carries no third-party intellectual-property infringement cover, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and no super-cap construct. The existing claim procedure in Section 6.3(b) (prompt notice, Servicer's right to assume the defense) is retained untouched, as is our own defend-title covenant in Section 9.2, which we do not flag. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-2438dd24","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"The agreement contains no licence grant: the only \"licen[cs]e\" references are regulatory qualification representations (p0234, p0259, p0272) and the Section 7.5(b) sentence at p0346, which disclaims any obligation on the Servicer to provide, license or assign its servicing software or applications. Because the AUDIT rule targets audits of our usage and no such right exists against us (and none grants the counterparty access to our systems), the position is better than preferred and we do not redline. Cellco, as Servicer and Custodian, services the Receivables and handles Obligor account and payment information, so the absence of coverage sits in walk-away territory. Article X (Miscellaneous) ends at Section 10.13, so we inserted a new Section 10.14 carrying only the fallback levels (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000). We selected the fallback rather than the preferred CGL/E&O/cyber/workers' compensation/certificates package as the shortest complete cure appropriate to this financing document.","proposal":"Insert a short insurance covenant (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000) as new Section 10.14 in Article X (Miscellaneous).","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-d81d8e15","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"The Agreement contains no intellectual property, deliverables or data-licence provision. Cellco's custody obligations (Section 3.10) confirm the Receivable Files are held for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee, and nothing purports to assign our IP or data to Cellco, so there is no walk-away issue. But the only IP-adjacent term, Section 7.5(b) (p0346), runs one way: it preserves the Servicer's processes, models and servicing software (acceptable as Vendor retention of its own tools and know-how) while leaving us with no licence at all in the Receivable Files, Monthly Investor Reports, records and other materials generated for us and stored on Cellco's receivables systems, and no limitation on the Servicer's use of our data. That fails the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business. We therefore add the shortest fallback clause alongside the existing transition provisions rather than upgrading to the preferred assignment construct, which would conflict with the Servicer's retained software rights.","proposal":"Add a fallback licence to Issuer deliverables and limit the Servicer's processing of Issuer data","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-1652befb","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"We searched the agreement, appendices and exhibits for MFN-style language (\"most favoured/favored nation\", \"no less favorable\", \"favorab\", \"favor\", comparable/third-party terms, right-to-match) and found none: every hit on \"favor\" is a security-interest grant in favour of the Issuer or Indenture Trustee. Servicer compensation in Section 3.8 is a fixed, defined Servicing Fee (plus Supplemental and Temporarily Excluded Receivables Servicing Fees) with no obligation on the Issuer, Depositor or the trust estate to extend Cellco terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, and no obligation to match or beat any third-party offer. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation burdening us), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-b259a839","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II TRANSFER AND ACQUISITION OF DEPOSITOR TRANSFERRED PROPERTY; REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES","rationale":"No take-or-pay, minimum purchase, volume-floor or shortfall-penalty obligation is imposed on the Issuer or the Depositor anywhere in the Agreement. Acquisitions of Additional Receivables under Section 2.1(b) occur only on an Acquisition Date, are conditioned on satisfaction of Section 2.1(d) (Transfer Notice, Credit Enhancement Test, Pool Composition Tests and Depositor certifications), and the Issuer's consideration is limited to the Additional Receivables Cash Transfer Amount for the Receivables actually transferred on that date — i.e., payment for assets actually acquired rather than a committed volume. Section 2.1(c) expressly confirms the Issuer assumes no other obligations. The Required Acquisition Deposit Amount and Required Negative Carry Amount constructs (p0225, p0398, p0564, p0927) are Revolving Period waterfall/credit-enhancement mechanics funded from the Issuer's own collections, not a purchase commitment; and the Credit Payment/shortfall deposit duty in Section 4.3(h) (p0211) runs against the Marketing Agent (counterparty side) and benefits us. This sits at the preferred position — no minimum commitment, with amounts payable only for assets actually acquired — so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-e36b19f0","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"Full-document searches for \"solicit\", \"employ or engage\", \"hire\"/\"no-hire\", \"induce\", \"recruit\", \"employment\", \"personnel\" and restrictive-covenant language return no responsive clause; the only reference to employees anywhere in the Transfer and Servicing Agreement is the indemnity definition of \"Indemnified Person\" in Section 6.3(i) (p0291), which imposes no hiring or solicitation restraint. The Issuer/Depositor (our party) are therefore under no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant, which meets the preferred position (\"No non-solicit on Customer\"). No redline is warranted; we would only need the fallback carve-outs (mutuality, services personnel only, 12 months, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach exclusions, no no-hire) if the Servicer/Marketing Agent later proposes adding such a covenant.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-57c46a06","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","rationale":"This transfer and servicing agreement contains no renewal mechanic at all. Because renewal is not automatic and no price increase is permitted, each conditional fallback element (60-day non-renewal window; 5% uplift cap) and each conditional preferred element (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, CPI/3% cap) is satisfied vacuously, and any extension of this self-liquidating term could only be effected by the parties amending the Agreement in writing under Section 10.4 (p0392) — i.e. by mutual written agreement, the preferred position. We have not pursued the preferred machine-readable-format and certified-deletion elements, and we leave the Section 7.5(b) carve-back for processes, models and servicing software untouched (that point sits with the IP rule).","proposal":"Add a 90-day transition assistance period and a 30-day outside date for delivery of the Receivable Files and records in Section 7.5.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-18b77328","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The Servicer's obligations run to a performance standard (Section 3.2(a): \\\"with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables\\\") and Section 6.1(a) contains point-in-time reps on compliance with Law and with the Servicing Procedures. That fails every fallback element, so we insert the shortest fallback warranty (90 days software conformance to documentation, 30 days services) with repair/replacement or refund.
